screens.name: Home — populated, unavailable, normal, 200%, transition
screens.evidence: Sheets 22–23 show complete daily content and dominant orb; supplied runtime reports Chrome/WebKit clearance, contrast and enlargement checks.
findings: Give the unavailable omen a clearer explanation of why returning tomorrow is the appropriate recovery.

screens.name: Approach — normal, large, transition
screens.evidence: Sheet 01 preserves the orb and opening message across variants, with the enlarged version switching to left-aligned copy.
findings: Keep the opening message alignment consistent with the centered ritual screens to strengthen transition continuity.

screens.name: Ask — myself, normal, large, transition
screens.evidence: Sheets 01 and 03 show labeled question input, disclosure and submit action, while the large view leaves the voice alternative partly below the viewport.
findings: Shorten the disclosure presentation so enlarged question entry keeps both submission and the voice alternative easier to discover.

screens.name: Ask — named person collapsed, normal, large, transition
screens.evidence: Sheet 02 shows the named subject above an unboxed question, with the large voice alternative touching the capture boundary.
findings: Give the unboxed question a clearer editable affordance consistent with the myself question state.

screens.name: Named-person editor — normal, large, transition
screens.evidence: Sheets 02–03 show selected Someone, labeled first-name input, privacy explanation and confirmation, with cancellation visible at normal size.
findings: Keep an explicit cancel-changes action readily discoverable at 200% as well as the global close control.

screens.name: Adaptive cards 1, 2 and 3 — normal, large, transitions
screens.evidence: Sheets 09–11 show numbered progression and four answers per card; runtime reports selected acknowledgement and duplicate prevention.
findings: Replace the vague first-card scale with choices that describe a consistent degree of preparation.

screens.name: Other-answer input — empty, populated, long answer, constrained viewport
screens.evidence: Sheets 11 and 19 show disabled empty submission and reachable populated submission; runtime reports retained long answers and returning choice focus.
findings: Replace the stale 'Write a few words to continue' instruction once a sufficient answer enables Reveal.

screens.name: Question entry — constrained viewport
screens.evidence: Sheet 19 shows the submit action and disclosure but only the bottom edge of the question field in the synthetic 500px viewport.
findings: Preserve a visible question label and useful portion of the typed question when the constrained viewport scrolls to submission.

screens.name: Planning and research — loading, large, transitions
screens.evidence: Sheets 34–35 distinguish checking from forming the forecast and expose cancellation; supplied evidence reports timeout, reduced-motion and cancellation checks.
findings: Retain the stage-specific explanation and charge reassurance through timeout and cancellation.

screens.name: Listening — voice-start failure, normal, large, transition
screens.evidence: Sheets 24–25 show microphone failure, a prominent typing fallback and voice retry, but the dominant headline remains a generic invitation.
findings: Make the failed voice state more prominent than the generic invitation so users immediately understand why typing is offered.

screens.name: Reading failures — planning and prediction, normal, large, transitions
screens.evidence: Sheets 14–15 show retry, question editing, prediction-stage answer review and explicit no-charge reassurance with readable enlarged layouts.
findings: Preserve the distinct recovery choices for failures before and after answers have been collected.

screens.name: Sensitive-question boundary — planning and prediction, normal, large, transitions
screens.evidence: Sheets 38–39 show a support action, alternatives and normal-size no-charge/no-memory reassurance; runtime reports sensitive-topic handling.
findings: Move the short no-charge/no-memory reassurance nearer the support explanation so it remains easier to encounter at 200%.

screens.name: Forecast reveal — normal, large, transition
screens.evidence: Sheets 36–38 show a speculative label, forecast, reminder date and strong share action; runtime reports actual reading, history and reminder flows.
findings: Reduce the visual competition from sharing so the forecast and its explanation remain the primary reading task.

screens.name: Evidence index — normal, large, transition
screens.evidence: Sheet 36 separates reasoning, answers, assumptions and sources with counts and chevrons, while also showing two routes back to the forecast.
findings: Clarify or consolidate the 'Back to forecast' and 'Read the forecast' controls to avoid competing return paths.

screens.name: Authored explanation — reason and limits, 100% and 200%
screens.evidence: Sheet 04 labels recorded context, scenario assumption and limits; runtime reports complete producer-authored sections and zero axe findings at both sizes.
findings: Keep the explicit lack-of-external-evidence statement adjacent to the scenario explanation.

screens.name: Evidence answers — normal, large, transition
screens.evidence: Sheet 16 pairs questions with lengthy synthetic answers and shows substantial scrolling at 200%.
findings: Give each question-answer group a stronger visual separation to support scanning long retained answers.

screens.name: Evidence assumptions — normal, large, transition
screens.evidence: Sheets 16–17 label assumptions explicitly and provide return navigation; the repeated and partial wording belongs to declared stress fixtures.
findings: Present multiple assumptions as separate readable units when longer real content contains more than one condition.

screens.name: Legacy explanation — evidence reason and reveal why, all sizes
screens.evidence: Sheets 17–18 and 37 use neutral Passage headings for dense legacy prose, with fixture content explicitly identified in the supplied evidence.
findings: Add a concise orientation explaining that Passage sections preserve an older explanation without assigning unsupported semantic roles.

screens.name: Evidence sources — normal, large, transition
screens.evidence: Sheet 18 distinguishes background sources from verification and shows publisher, date, long synthetic excerpts and external links.
findings: Place each source-opening action nearer its identifying information so long excerpts do not bury the action.

screens.name: Check-in — initial, forecast collapsed and expanded, all sizes
screens.evidence: Sheets 12–13 and 29–30 retain the original question and forecast disclosure; the expanded large forecast pushes outcome choices below the viewport.
findings: Keep a visible route to the outcome choices when an enlarged forecast is expanded.

screens.name: Check-in — saved yes, no and pending, normal and 200%
screens.evidence: Sheets 30–32 show explicit Saved messages and checkmarks; runtime reports persistence, correction, pressed state and unchanged reminders for all outcomes.
findings: Keep the pending-specific explanation that the reading remains open and the reminder stays unchanged.

screens.name: History — empty, normal, large, transition
screens.evidence: Sheets 20–21 show a clear empty state, local-storage explanation and Ask the Ball action across text sizes.
findings: Retain the direct action from the empty state into the first reading.

screens.name: History — populated, stress list and persisted outcome
screens.evidence: Sheets 20–21 distinguish question, forecast, reminder and saved outcome, while the enlarged single row puts its opening action below the visible fold.
findings: Bring the row-opening affordance closer to its date or question so enlarged entries remain easy to act on.

screens.name: Sky — offline samples, selected topic, normal, large, transition
screens.evidence: Sheets 44–45 show labeled sample content, retry and selected Love, with the constellation becoming a text grid at 200%.
findings: Tighten the enlarged offline notice and category spacing so the selected sample question becomes visible sooner.

screens.name: Circles — offline, normal, large, transition
screens.evidence: Sheets 13–14 truthfully show offline status, retry and unavailable controls, but repeat the circle-sharing explanation in two sections.
findings: Combine the repeated circle introduction and sharing explanation to shorten the offline screen, especially at 200%.

screens.name: Age confirmation — normal, large, transition
screens.evidence: Sheet 25 shows clearly differentiated age choices; supplied runtime cites age guards but the phrase 'Teen-safe defaults' remains unexplained.
findings: Replace 'Teen-safe defaults apply' with a short user-facing description of what changes.

screens.name: Birthday onboarding — optional, normal, large, transition
screens.evidence: Sheet 26 shows optional birthday fields, Continue and Skip with heading focus, while stacked enlarged fields move both actions below the viewport.
findings: Place a visible skip action near the optional label so enlarged users need not traverse all fields to decline.

screens.name: Age blocked and birthday correction — normal, large, transitions
screens.evidence: Sheets 26–28 show the age restriction and explicit correction route; runtime cites age-guard and focus checks.
findings: Reduce vertical spacing in the enlarged correction form while preserving doubled text so its check action is reached sooner.

screens.name: Focus onboarding — unselected and selected, all sizes
screens.evidence: Sheets 28–29 show optional choices, a selected checkmark and changing continuation copy, with the large continuation button cut by the capture boundary.
findings: Shorten the enlarged introductory stack so the continuation action is more discoverable after selecting a focus.

screens.name: You — profile, memory and plan summary, normal, large, transition
screens.evidence: Sheets 47–48 organize birth profile, plan and editable memory, with the large first viewport consumed mainly by profile content.
findings: Reduce the enlarged gaps between profile actions so memory and plan management are discovered sooner.

screens.name: Birthday editing — normal, 200% and transition
screens.evidence: Sheets 24 and 47 show labeled date fields, save, cancellation and birthday removal, with the large save action beyond the first viewport.
findings: Keep save and cancellation closely attached to the final date field throughout enlarged scrolling.

screens.name: Birth details — initial and editing, normal, 200%, transition
screens.evidence: Sheets 05–07 and 46 show optional time and city inputs, disabled save and explanatory text; runtime reports keyboard/focus and exact input scaling.
findings: Reduce repeated helper-copy spacing so enlarged users encounter city selection and the save requirement sooner.

screens.name: Birth details — live city results and invalid time
screens.evidence: Sheet 07 shows disambiguated city results and precise time validation; runtime reports real lookup, validation focus and zero axe findings.
findings: Retain geographic disambiguation and the explicit valid time range in every text-size variant.

screens.name: Birth details — no results, service failure and retry
screens.evidence: Sheets 05 and 08 distinguish unavailable search from no matching city and show recovery; runtime reports controlled failures and actual retry.
findings: Preserve separate recovery wording for changing a city query versus retrying an unavailable service.

screens.name: Birth profile — calculated, saved, retried and forgotten
screens.evidence: Sheets 06 and 08 show saved location/time, edit and forget actions, plus confirmation that forgetting preserves the birthday.
findings: Use consistent capitalization for displayed sign names to polish the saved profile.

screens.name: Settings — normal and large controls
screens.evidence: Sheets 39–40 show labeled switches and management actions; runtime reports reduced-motion behavior and exact enlargement.
findings: Maintain a clear grouping boundary between preferences, plan/privacy links and the destructive forget action.

screens.name: Plans — annual and monthly selected, normal, large, transitions
screens.evidence: Sheets 33–34 disclose billing cadence, totals and simulation, with selected checks; runtime reports monthly aria-checked verification.
findings: Make reading-pack alternatives easier to discover in the enlarged layout after the subscription action.

screens.name: Sharing — default and expanded options, normal, large, transitions
screens.evidence: Sheets 40–44 show preview, image-text access, enlargement, download and privacy explanation, with invite tools below the main export section.
findings: Bring the image-text and enlargement affordances into a tighter group with the preview to reduce vertical travel.

screens.name: Sharing — preparing, failed export and completed download
screens.evidence: Sheets 40–43 show preparing, retry and download-started states; runtime reports held encoding, duplicate prevention, failure recovery and a real PNG download.
findings: Retain the precise 'download started' wording rather than implying that the user has saved or shared the file.

screens.name: Shared-image inspection and story — normal, large, transitions
screens.evidence: Sheets 41 and 45–46 show enlarged portrait artwork and a return action; supplied evidence reports full-resolution export and return focus.
findings: Keep direct access to the scalable text equivalent available from image inspection as well as the sharing screen.

screens.name: Share image text — normal, large, transition
screens.evidence: Sheets 43–44 provide scalable forecast, speculative qualification, brand text and a download action above the artwork.
findings: Add a little separation between the download button and artwork so the action does not visually merge with the image frame.

components.name: Hero orb
components.evidence: Home and ritual sheets show a consistent illustrated glass orb; runtime reports size bounds, motion performance and reduced-motion checks.
findings: Keep the visible invitation attached to the interactive Home orb so its action does not rely on illustration alone.

components.name: Tab bar
components.evidence: Main-screen sheets show five labeled destinations, selected underlines and a raised Ask orb; runtime reports target-size and clearance checks.
findings: Keep the raised Ask orb from visually competing with content immediately above the bar at 200%.

components.name: Wordmark and balance header
components.evidence: Headers consistently show the brand or page title and remaining readings, with balances wrapping to two lines at 200%.
findings: Reduce the balance underline's visual emphasis so the utility counter remains subordinate to page content.

components.name: Primary button
components.evidence: The cream filled button is consistent across screens, with enabled, disabled, loading and retry examples supported by runtime target checks.
findings: Preserve full multiline labels and the same enabled/disabled distinction across enlarged variants.

components.name: Secondary action
components.evidence: Secondary actions alternate between gold links and centered white row labels throughout sharing, profile, recovery and reading screens.
findings: Assign gold links and white action rows consistent roles so users can predict their importance.

components.name: Answer choice
components.evidence: Card choices use separated full-width rows; runtime reports selected acknowledgement, duplicate prevention and 44px minimum controls.
findings: Make answer wording parallel within each set so selection requires less interpretation.

components.name: Question input
components.evidence: Ask screens show labeled serif question fields and strong focus outlines, but the collapsed named-person field appears unboxed.
findings: Use a consistent editable boundary for both myself and named-person questions.

components.name: Large-text and constrained input
components.evidence: Sheet 19 retains long answer text and reachable submit controls, but constrained question entry shows almost none of the question field.
findings: Keep enough focused input and its label visible to preserve context alongside the submit action.

components.name: Settings switch
components.evidence: Sheets 39–40 show labeled off/on switches, and runtime reports reduced-motion behavior, doubling and control target checks.
findings: Retain the full labeled row as the accessible activation target around the compact switch graphic.

components.name: Omen content
components.evidence: Sheets 22–23 show complete unframed daily content and two-line unavailability; runtime reports populated and unavailable bounds at both sizes.
findings: Explain the unavailable state enough to justify the tomorrow-only recovery instruction.

components.name: Sky stars and selected question
components.evidence: Sheet 45 uses labeled stars and a selected checkmark, while sheet 44 replaces the star arrangement with a readable enlarged grid.
findings: Preserve a stronger visual connection between the selected topic and its question after the layout becomes a grid.

components.name: Circle surface
components.evidence: Sheets 13–14 distinguish offline status and disabled creation/eligibility but repeat the privacy and sharing proposition.
findings: Remove the duplicate explanation and keep the offline reason adjacent to the unavailable action.

components.name: History row
components.evidence: Sheets 20–21 show date, original question, forecast, reminder or outcome and an explicit check-in link.
findings: Position the opening affordance earlier in the row so long enlarged forecasts do not bury it.

components.name: Plan option
components.evidence: Sheets 33–34 show annual and monthly prices, billing periods and selection marks; runtime reports checked-state verification.
findings: Keep the total charge visually tied to billing frequency when options stack at 200%.

components.name: Share preview
components.evidence: Sharing sheets show a small portrait preview whose text needs enlargement, with separate image-text and full-image views.
findings: Increase useful preview text size or place its text-equivalent action immediately beside it.

components.name: Notice and recovery
components.evidence: Birth search, reading error and export states distinguish failure types and provide specific retry or editing actions supported by runtime checks.
findings: Apply the same specific recovery standard to Home's less explanatory unavailable state.

components.name: Typography system
components.evidence: The deck consistently pairs expressive serif headings with sans-serif utility text, while enlarged forms and evidence pages become vertically dense.
findings: Tune enlarged spacing and long-heading roles without reducing the verified 200% text multiplier.

components.name: Atmospheric background
components.evidence: The sheets maintain a borderless dark mist and restrained gold glow; runtime reports rendered contrast and isolated motion checks.
findings: Keep the calm text zones and reduced-motion treatment as atmospheric effects evolve.

components.name: Birthday input
components.evidence: Birthday screens use explicit day/month/year labels, examples and stacked enlargement; supplied evidence reports age guards and input scaling.
findings: Reduce enlarged inter-field spacing so the date and its confirmation remain a cohesive task.

components.name: Age confirmation
components.evidence: Sheet 25 gives two explicit age choices and supplied runtime cites guarded continuation and correction.
findings: Explain the user-visible effect of the stated teen defaults in plain language.

components.name: Focus selection
components.evidence: Sheets 28–29 show optional selection, a non-color checkmark and a corresponding continuation-label change.
findings: Keep the confirmation action easier to discover beneath enlarged choices.

components.name: Birth-profile surface
components.evidence: Sheets 06, 08 and 48 distinguish saved chart details, editable birthday and precise forget confirmation.
findings: Standardize sign-name capitalization across the Sun, Moon and rising summaries.

components.name: Birth-details form
components.evidence: Sheets 05–08 cover initial, validation, search, failure, saved and forgotten states supported by actual lookup and persistence evidence.
findings: Keep selection prerequisites and validation beside their inputs while reducing repeated vertical helper spacing.

components.name: Named-person control
components.evidence: Sheets 02–03 show subject switching, selected Someone, labeled name entry and a nobody-notified explanation.
findings: Add explicit browser evidence for cancelling and reopening the editor while preserving the original subject and question.

components.name: Evidence disclosure
components.evidence: Check-in and evidence sheets show chevron disclosure, visible focus and explicit section labels; runtime reports keyboard operation and full content.
findings: Use consistent labels for opening reasoning, opening the forecast and returning to the forecast.

components.name: Export status
components.evidence: Sheets 40–43 place preparing, failure and download-started text next to the button, backed by controlled encoder and download tests.
findings: Preserve the distinct pending, retryable failure and download-started messages with the same nearby placement.

components.name: Full-screen modal navigation
components.evidence: Reading, evidence and sharing screens combine a global close icon with contextual back links; supplied evidence covers return focus for selected flows.
findings: Verify and document consistent close-versus-back destinations across every nested full-screen view.

limitations: This is a provisional browser assessment of the supplied screenshots and runtime narrative; no independent browser drive, source inspection or additional artifact inspection was performed.
Scores use the six frozen dimensions; A is the mean of hierarchy, typography and surfaces, F is the mean of clarity, feedback and accessibility, and overall is 0.4A + 0.6F.
Null marks genuinely inapplicable dimensions for decorative or noninteractive components; missing interaction evidence is reflected in provisional numeric scores.
Corresponding transitions are grouped with settled screens; still images support visual continuity judgments but cannot independently establish animation timing or interaction behavior.
Content below a screenshot boundary is not treated as unreachable: supplied runtime reports scrolling and layout checks, although several first-view compositions remain weak at 200%.
The constrained 500px views demonstrate synthetic viewport handling, not native keyboard behavior.
Runtime assertions about tests, focus, targets, contrast, motion, persistence and exports are supplied evidence rather than checks independently repeated by this evaluator.
Synthetic layout answers, sources and error wording are not treated as production-copy defects or evidence of model quality.
Legacy moderate-confidence wording remains in historical fixtures; it provides no evidence of calibration or migration.
Circles is visibly offline in this preview; current connected social behavior and production authentication are not demonstrated by these sheets.
Physical iPhone, native text enlargement, VoiceOver, microphone, haptics, real payments and OS sharing remain unverified; browser scores of 9 do not certify those boundaries.
No novice-user study or representative physical accessibility study is supplied, so no score of 10 is awarded.
No supplied evidence establishes a hard-gate failure, but the authorized A>=9 and F>=9 threshold is not met across all screens and components.
topFixes: Preserve question context in the constrained entry viewport; the shown submit position leaves almost the entire question input out of view.
Improve 200% task composition through shorter copy and tighter spacing, especially birthday onboarding, focus selection, profile forms and expanded check-in.
Unify editable-question affordances and the roles of gold links, white action rows and contextual return controls.
Reduce repeated Circles copy and clarify Home's unavailable-omen recovery.
Improve long-content scanning and action placement in evidence sources and enlarged history rows.
Keep share previews, scalable image text and enlargement actions closely grouped, with direct text access from inspection.
